title: Splitting a pie
objectives: Solve ultimatum and alternating-offer bargaining games.

screens.title: A shrinking pie
screens.prose: Ana and Ben split £100. Ana proposes a split. If Ben refuses, the pie shrinks by 10% and Ben proposes. If Ana refuses, it shrinks again and Ana makes a final offer. A refusal of the final offer leaves both with nothing. An indifferent responder accepts.
screens.question: Fill in what each proposer keeps, from round 3 up.

hints.text: Start with round 3: Ben must accept anything, so Ana keeps it all.
In round 2 Ana accepts any offer worth at least the £81 she would get in round 3.
Round 3: 81. Round 2: Ben offers 81, keeps 9. Round 1: Ana offers Ben 9, keeps 91.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work up from round 3: each responder accepts what refusing would bring.

byKey.r0c3: Ben will accept £9 in round 1, since refusing brings him £9 in round 2. Ana keeps the other £91.
byKey.r1c3: Ben must offer Ana £81, what she gets by refusing. Of £90 that leaves him £9.

explain.text: In round 3 Ana keeps all £81. So in round 2 Ben must offer Ana £81 of £90, keeping £9. So in round 1 Ana offers Ben £9 and keeps £91; Ben accepts at once.

screens.title: One round only
screens.prose: Cut the game to one round, the **ultimatum game**. Ana proposes a split of £100; Ben accepts, or refuses and both get nothing. An indifferent Ben accepts.
screens.question: What does Ana offer Ben?

options.why: You picked the fair split. Refusing gives Ben nothing, so in theory any offer is enough.
That is the answer when Ben refuses a zero offer and money comes in whole pounds. Here an indifferent Ben accepts £0.

hints.text: What does Ben get if he refuses?
An indifferent Ben accepts: Ana offers £0.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare each offer with what refusing brings Ben.

byKey.b: You picked the fair split. Refusing gives Ben nothing, so in theory any offer is enough.

explain.text: Refusing brings Ben £0, so any offer of at least £0 is accepted, and Ana keeps £100. In whole pounds with a Ben who refuses £0, she keeps £99. Real responders often refuse small offers: the theory says what is safe, not what people do.

screens.title: More rounds
screens.prose: Keep δ = 0.9: each refusal shrinks the pie to 0.9 of its size. Shares are of the first-round pie, with Ana proposing in round 1.
screens.question: Fill in Ana's share for each number of rounds.

hints.text: Adding a round in front: Ana keeps 1 minus 0.9 times the next proposer's share.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each extra round gives $1 - 0.9 \times$ the share with one round fewer.

explain.text: Each extra round in front gives the proposer $1 - 0.9s$, where $s$ is the next proposer's share. The shares swing 0.1, 0.91, 0.181, 0.8371, closing in on a middle value. That value solves $s = 1 - 0.9s$: $\tfrac{1}{1.9} = 0.5263$.

screens.title: Unequal patience
screens.prose: With no last round, Ana discounts by $\delta_A$ and Ben by $\delta_B$ per round. Let $x$ be Ana's share when she proposes and $y$ Ben's share when he proposes.
screens.question: Put the derivation in order. Leave out the line that does not belong.

lines.text: Ben accepts the least that matches waiting to propose: $1 - x = \delta_B\, y$.
Ana accepts the least that matches waiting to propose: $1 - y = \delta_A\, x$.
Ben accepts the least that matches waiting: $1 - x = \delta_A\, y$.
lines.why: Ben waits at his own rate, $\delta_B$. Ana's patience does not shrink what he expects.

hints.text: Each responder accepts what refusing and proposing next is worth to them.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write each responder's indifference with their own discount.

byKey.d1: Ben waits at his own rate, $\delta_B$. Ana's patience does not shrink what he expects.
byKey.left-out: Every line but the one with the wrong discount belongs.

explain.text: Each responder is offered exactly what proposing next round is worth to them. Solving the two lines gives $x = \tfrac{1 - \delta_B}{1 - \delta_A \delta_B}$. With equal $\delta$ this is $\tfrac{1}{1 + \delta}$.

screens.title: The patient side
screens.prose: Ana discounts by $\delta_A = 0.9$ a round and Ben by $\delta_B = 0.8$. Ana proposes first, with no last round.
screens.question: What share does Ana get?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Put $\delta_A = 0.9$ and $\delta_B = 0.8$ into the formula.

byKey.equal: That is the equal-patience share at 0.9. Ben is less patient here, so Ana gets more.
byKey.swap: You swapped the factors: $\tfrac{1 - 0.9}{0.28}$. The numerator uses Ben's $\delta_B$.

explain.text: Ana's share is $\tfrac{1 - 0.8}{1 - 0.72} = \tfrac{0.2}{0.28} = 0.7143$. Ben's impatience costs him: he takes 0.2857. Patience is bargaining power.

screens.title: No last round
screens.prose: Back to equal patience, δ = 0.9 for both. There is no last round: offers can go back and forth for ever.
screens.question: What share does the first proposer get?

options.why: You split fairly. Proposing first is worth something: Ben would lose a tenth of the pie by refusing.
That is the pie left after one round. Ben refuses anything below what his own proposal is worth.
That is the two-round answer. With no last round the swings settle in the middle.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the share that stays the same when a round is added.

byKey.b: You split fairly. Proposing first is worth something: Ben would lose a tenth of the pie by refusing.

explain.text: With no last round, every round looks the same, so the proposer's share $s$ satisfies $s = 1 - 0.9s$. That gives $\tfrac{1}{1.9} = 52.63\%$. The edge from proposing first is small when the pie shrinks slowly.

screens.title: A pie that vanishes
screens.prose: Take δ = 0 with no last round: after one refusal the pie is gone.
screens.question: What does the first proposer keep?

options.text: All of it: this is the ultimatum game

options.why: Half needs a responder with something to lose by accepting less. Refusing brings Ben nothing.
The proposer keeps everything; it is the responder who gets nothing.

hints.text: What is waiting worth to Ben when δ = 0?
Nothing: the pie is gone after one refusal.
So Ana keeps it all; the formula gives $\tfrac{1}{1 + 0} = 1$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask what refusing brings Ben.

byKey.b: Half needs a responder with something to lose by accepting less. Refusing brings Ben nothing.

explain.text: With δ = 0 a refusal leaves nothing, so this is the ultimatum game. Ana keeps the whole pie, and the formula agrees: $\tfrac{1}{1 + 0} = 1$. The other edge, δ near 1, gives an even split.

screens.title: Work back from the last round
screens.prose:
A responder accepts any offer worth at least what rejecting would bring. With a common factor δ and no last round, the first proposer gets

$$x = \frac{1}{1 + \delta}, \qquad \text{and with unequal factors } x = \frac{1 - \delta_B}{1 - \delta_A\delta_B}.$$
screens.question: With δ = 0.99 and no last round, about what share does the first proposer get?

options.why: That is the pie left after a round. The responder can wait almost for free, so the split is nearly even.
The proposer keeps more than half, not less, since the responder loses a little by waiting.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Put δ = 0.99 into $\tfrac{1}{1 + \delta}$.

explain.text: $\tfrac{1}{1.99} = 0.5025$. When waiting costs almost nothing, proposing first is worth almost nothing. When waiting is costly, the proposer takes more.

screens.title: Drill
screens.prose: Four splits, about three minutes each, as an interview allows. Say the reasoning aloud before you answer. Ana always proposes first. Give her share as a percentage.
screens.question: Fill in Ana's share in each game.

hints.text: Finite games: work back. Infinite: use the formulas.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Check the first answer that is marked.

explain.text: Two rounds leave Ana $1 - 0.8 = 20\%$, and three rounds $1 - 0.8 \times 0.2 = 84\%$. With no last round, $\tfrac{1}{1.8} = 55.56\%$. With unequal factors, $\tfrac{0.1}{0.145} = 68.97\%$.

screens.title: Follow-up: an outside offer
screens.prose: The interviewer gives Ben an outside offer, £30 and then £60, of a £100 pie. He can take it instead of answering Ana. δ = 0.9 for both and there is no last round.
screens.question: How much does Ana keep in each case, in £?

hints.text: Ben takes the outside offer only if it beats what he expects in the game.
£30 changes nothing: 52.63. £60 binds: Ana offers 60 and keeps 40.

feedback.correct: £52.63 with the £30 offer, £40 with the £60 offer.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare each outside offer with what Ben already expects.

byKey.r0c1: £30 is less than the £47.37 Ben expects anyway, so it is not a threat. Ana still keeps £52.63.
byKey.r1c1: £60 beats Ben's £47.37, so Ana must offer exactly £60 and keeps £40.

explain.text: Ben already expects £47.37, so a £30 outside offer changes nothing. A £60 offer binds: Ana offers exactly £60 and keeps £40 (both checked over 2,000 rounds). In a block-trade negotiation the side with no deadline has δ near 1 and takes the larger share.

ideas: Work back from the last round: a responder accepts any offer worth at least what rejecting would bring.
With a common factor δ and no last round, the first proposer gets $\tfrac{1}{1 + \delta}$.
The more patient side takes more: $\tfrac{1 - \delta_B}{1 - \delta_A\delta_B}$ for Ana.

formula.name: Alternating offers
formula.note: Ana proposes first; with equal factors it is $\tfrac{1}{1 + \delta}$.

summary.trap: Answering 50% from fairness. Proposing first is worth something whenever waiting costs.

quiz.prose: Ana proposes a split of a pie. If Ben refuses, it shrinks to 0.6 of its size and Ben makes a final offer.
quiz.question: What share does Ana get, as a percentage?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ana must offer Ben what refusing brings him.

byKey.sixty: 0.6 is what Ben gets by refusing. Ana offers him that and keeps the rest.

explain.text: If Ben refuses he keeps the whole shrunk pie, 0.6. So Ana offers 0.6 and keeps 0.4, which is 40%.

quiz.prose: Alternating offers with no last round and δ = 0.5 for both. Ana proposes first.
quiz.question: What share does Ana get, as a percentage?

byKey.half: That is δ itself. The proposer's share is $\tfrac{1}{1 + \delta}$.

explain.text: With no last round the proposer gets $\tfrac{1}{1 + 0.5} = \tfrac23$, about 66.67%. Waiting halves the pie, so Ben accepts a third.

quiz.prose: Alternating offers with no last round. Ana's patience stays fixed while Ben becomes more patient: $\delta_B$ rises.
quiz.question: What happens to Ana's share?

options.why: A more patient Ben loses less by refusing, so he holds out for more.
Ana's share $\tfrac{1 - \delta_B}{1 - \delta_A\delta_B}$ depends on Ben's patience.

feedback.correct: It falls: patience is bargaining power.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask what refusing costs a more patient Ben.

explain.text: A more patient Ben loses less by waiting, so he accepts only a larger offer. Ana's share $\tfrac{1 - \delta_B}{1 - \delta_A\delta_B}$ falls as $\delta_B$ rises. Patience is bargaining power.
